blocks.review: 第一套 本作文的要求是，假设校报正在为其下一期内容征稿，征稿主题是“最令人印象深刻的校园活动”，考 生需要围绕这一主题进行投稿。写作时应展开介绍，着力从活动的具体内容、意义等方面进行陈述。此外，应 注意写作句式和用语的多样性，使文章更有层次，表达更丰富。
blocks.sample: Among a variety of campus events, the new year's EveGala stands out as a remarkableoccasionthathasleftanenduring mark on my university experience.1 This celebration captured the essence of cultural richness and community spirit, bringing together students from various backgrounds in an atmosphere of shared joy.2 The gala beg an with traditionalperformances, showing the diversity of Chinese culture. From fascinating dances, such as the elegant movements of classical chinese dance, to wonderful musical performances featuring traditional instruments likeGuzhengandPipa, the event became akaleidoscope of artistic expressions.4 As students participated in interactive activitieslike group performances and fun party games, the enthusiasm of everyone on site was mobilized, and the party reached its climax. In conclusion, the New Year's Eve Gala goes beyond mere entertainment; it serves as a powerful symbol of cultural diversity on our campus. Reflecting on this event, I'm reminded of the harmonious blend oftraditions and modernity that defines our university experience.6

blocks.sampleCn: 在各种各样的校园活动中，“元旦联欢晚会”是一场引人注目的盛会，给我的大学经历留下了不可磨 灭的印记。这一庆祝活动抓住了文化丰富性和社区精神的精髓，将来自不同背景的学生聚集在一个共享欢 乐的氛围中。 元旦联欢晚会以传统表演拉开帷幕，展示了中国文化的多样性。从迷人的舞蹈，如中国古典舞的优雅 动作，到以古筝和琵琶等传统乐器为特色的精彩的音乐表演，这场活动成为艺术表达的万花筒。当学生们 参加集体表演和趣味派对游戏等互动环节时，现场所有人的积极性都被调动起来，晚会达到了高潮。 总之，元旦联欢晚会不仅仅是娱乐活动，它也是我们校园文化多样性的有力象征。回想这一活动，我 便会想起传统与现代的和谐融合，这定义了我们的大学体验。

blocks.analysisOverview: 本文节选自Equitable（美国领先的金融服务公司之一）公司官网2020年9月1日发布的一篇题为“Just 10MinutesofExercisea WeekMay Be Enoughto Extend Your Life，Study Says”的文章。文章围绕一项关于 “每周只锻炼10分钟就能延长寿命”的研究结果展开论述。
blocks.translationCn: 根据发表在《英国运动医学杂志》上的一项新研究，每周只锻炼10分钟就有助于延年益寿。 最近的一些研究发现，即使是短时间的低强度运动，也能对健康产生重要[26]影响。尽管如此，每周只锻 炼10分钟可能就足以延长寿命的想法还是很新颖的。这也有一定的[27争议性，因为联邦体育活动指南建议每 周至少进行75分钟的剧烈运动或150分钟的[28]适度运动。 该研究基于1997年至2008年间[29]参加全国健康访谈调查的88,000多名美国成年人的数据。 一些研究发现，健康的运动量是有[30]上限的，与此相反，该研究的研究人员发现，运动对长寿的好处 [31]似乎没有上限。即使运动量是联邦政府建议的10倍的那一小群人，其死亡[32]风险也比运动量最小的人群 低46%。 不过，像这样的观察性研究并不能证明因果关系；它们只能发现[33]规律。研究人员也无法[34]调整某些 可能影响寿命的生活方式因素，包括饮食习惯和体育锻炼随时间的变化。尽管存在这些[35]局限性，但这项研 究的结果再次表明了体育锻炼的影响，即使是少量的体育锻炼。

blocks.material: One of my bad habits is saying "busy”when people ask me how I'm doing. Sometimes it’s because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that’s what i think i'm supposed to say. That’s what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say. But working long hours doesn't drive better results. Never taking a vacation won't lead to a promotion. So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time? In 2016,researchers from columbia, Harvard, andGeorgetownconducted a study to figure it out. They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influencedby our ownbeliefs about social mobility. In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success base don hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are ofhigher standing. That's why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there's a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails, and stress, then they're probably a big deal. This culture ofbusyness is making it hard for ·2023年12月四级真题（第一套）· 6 ===== PAGE 7 ===== employees to find work-life balance. According to are cent study, one in five highlyengaged employees is at risk of burn out(精疲力竭). Personally, I'm going to stop saying "busy”when people ask me how I am. It sounds self-righteous（自以 为是的) andsets the wrong tone.
